# Monster Battle 9001: Voice Script

<!-- Generated by tools/audio/voice/build.sh (mbvoice/scriptdoc.py). Edit the script files, not this page. -->

Every spoken line in the game. Since round 4 (`docs/ROADMAP.md`) the game says nothing by itself except one thing: the news tells the monster's player that the creature can molt. Everything else is talk the players choose with the **communication rose** (hold the rose key, pick a wedge, let go): the army shouts schlocky 1950s monster-movie radio nonsense, the monster roars, snuffles and sings (its noises are sound effects, not lines: `docs/audio/SFX.md`). None of it changes the game.

- **2 news line(s)** for the monster's molt, in `shared/src/defs/voiceLines.json`.
- **8 army wedges** with their lines in `client/src/audio/roseLines.json`. Every sentence is spoken in each of the 4 squad voices (Granite, Beacon, Tempest, Anvil), so the 40 sentences make 160 sound files, `rose_<voice>_<wedge>_<number>`. A player's squad always speaks in its own voice; the subtitle shows the player's name and the words.
- A later pass with a commercial voice service can rebuild every file from the same two files: change the voices in `tools/audio/voice/cast.json` (or replace `mbvoice/synth.py`) and run `tools/audio/voice/build.sh --force`.

## Rules for writing new lines

The build checks all of these and refuses to run when one is broken (`tools/audio/voice/mbvoice/scriptcheck.py`).

- A rose line is **one sentence**, at most 12 words, shouted: it ends with one exclamation mark (the voices get more of them when spoken, which the build adds). A wedge has 4 to 6 lines.
- The tone: an absurd world played completely straight. Earnest, inane, never mean, nothing gory, nothing about any real faith.
- Only letters, spaces, commas, periods and exclamation marks; no apostrophes (say "it is", not "it's"); every word in the speech recognizer's dictionary, so the build can check that it is heard; no word that can be said two ways ("live", "close", "wind", "upset"); no words in capitals (they would be spelled out).
- Try a wording first: `tools/audio/voice/tryline.py Granite "Your line here!"` speaks it in that voice and chain and prints what the recognizer hears.
- A new wedge needs a picture and its place at the end of `ROSE_ARMY` in `shared/src/net/rose.ts`.

In the last build the modern speech recognizer heard 143 of 162 finished lines word for word (`docs/audio/VOICE.md` has the details).
